column1: Pour the water into a large bowl, add the salt, and stir by hand until it dissolves.
Mix in 100g of the flour until it forms a thin batter, then rub in the yeast with your fingers until it dissolves.
Add the remaining flour a little at a time, mixing with one hand while turning the bowl with the other.
When the dough comes together, turn it onto the counter and knead with both hands until it absorbs all the flour and feels smooth.
Check it is ready: it should spring back when poked and read 73–79°F (23–26°C) in the center.
Cover with a damp cloth and rest at least 2 hours.
Divide into 250g (8.8 oz) pieces and roll each under your palm into a smooth, tight ball.
Place the balls in a flat airtight container and proof 24 hours at 61–64°F (16–18°C).
On a floured counter, press each ball out from the center with your fingertips, leaving a raised rim, then flip and repeat. Stretch gently over your forearm into a round.
Top as desired and bake in a 752°F (400°C) wood-fired oven, or a home oven at maximum heat with a pizza stone, turning once so it cooks evenly.
